rationale: Mór-hop refers to a moorland pool or marshy body of standing water, as evidenced by its use in Beowulf (B. 450) in the context of the desolate, boggy terrain associated with Grendel's lair. The compound's first element *mór* (moor/marsh) and the Beowulf context point to a small, stagnant body of standing water on moorland, which best matches pool.n.06 (a small body of standing water), rather than an excavated pool (pool.n.01) or a larger lake (pond.n.01).
